short: Gas turbine, composite armour, and the tank the US Army has fielded since 1980.
full:
The M1 entered US Army service in 1980, the American half of the settlement after the MBT-70 programme failed. It used a 1,500 hp Honeywell gas turbine, quiet and powerful but thirsty, and British-derived Chobham composite armour. The first version kept the 105 mm rifled gun; the M1A1 of 1985 switched to the German 120 mm smoothbore and added depleted uranium mesh in the armour from 1988.

Its reputation was made in Kuwait and Iraq in February 1991, where Abrams crews using thermal sights destroyed Iraqi T-72s at ranges beyond which their opponents could see, let alone shoot; almost no Abrams were lost to enemy tank fire. Urban fighting in Iraq after 2003 was harder, and mines and shaped-charge IEDs destroyed a number of them. Successive M1A2 SEP upgrades keep it current, and the type serves with Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Australia, Poland and, since 2023, Ukraine.
